correctness.rationale: Tame genus-five cover and character eigenspaces give five genus-one factors; the composite norm/pullback is [8] and hence the isogeny is prime to 7. H_7(lambda)=(lambda+1)(lambda-2)(lambda-4) gives harmonic criterion. Pairwise quartet intersection plus PGL2(F7) triple transitivity proves s belongs to {0,1,3}; five incidence counts give exact formulas for all q=7^n. The standalone exact checker confirms q=7,49 and Hasse roots, but infinity relies on algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: Known five-elliptic decomposition is explicitly credited. The novel candidate is the sharp characteristic-seven arithmetic restriction s in {0,1,3}, equivalently missing p-rank 3, together with Newton strata and exact marked counts. Full text of most directly relevant 2015 preprint, 2014 model paper and 2017 characteristic-three comparison was inspected where relevant. Inaccessible older full text and unindexed historical finite-geometry results remain risks.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not certified; the 2008 Yamauchi article could not be examined beyond its abstract.
Classical projective finite-geometry literature on harmonic five-point configurations may contain an equivalent incidence theorem under different terminology.
The 2015 geometric decomposition is a complex-analytic published input but the present proof independently establishes a prime-to-seven correspondence to transfer p-divisible groups.

value.rationale: A complete natural two-dimensional genus-five family is stratified by rank, a-number and Newton slopes in characteristic seven, with a nonobvious forbidden rank and a unique extremal projective branch orbit; exact marked parameter counts hold for every finite extension. These identify natural arithmetic moduli invariants and a nontrivial supersingular compatibility constraint, rather than a hand-picked finite computation.
